result_text:
`Tool.from_function` and `FunctionTool.from_function` now use the metadata a `@tool`-decorated function carries, as long as you pass no `metadata=` and no individual metadata arguments. Your `greet` example now gives `name` "custom-greet", `description` "Greets people", `version` "v1", `title`, `tags` and `meta` as given to the decorator.

The change is one block in `FunctionTool.from_function` in `src/fastmcp/tools/function_tool.py`. It picks up `__fastmcp__` only when it is a `ToolMeta`. `Tool.from_function` calls `FunctionTool.from_function`, so it behaves the same way. Every `ToolMeta` field is used, not only the ones you listed.

The existing behaviour is unchanged. An explicit `metadata=` or any individual argument is used as before, with no merging. Passing both still raises the same `TypeError`. Undecorated functions, and functions whose `__fastmcp__` isn't a `ToolMeta`, behave as before.

I ran your example and `tests/tools`. 305 tests passed, 1 was skipped, and 1 failed: `test_default_threadpool_permits_concurrency` in `test_tool_run_in_thread.py`. That test passed when I re-ran its file on its own, so it looks timing-related under `-n auto`. I didn't run the full suite or the lint checks. I also didn't add a test for the new behaviour.

The sandbox blocked the shell at first, so I ran the commands outside it.
